headline: Chips Surge as Software Stumbles; Geopolitical Fog Hangs Over the Week Ahead
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a divided note, with 300 names advancing against 241 decliners across a 545-stock universe. Semiconductors led all sectors by a wide margin, climbing 3.05%, as Sandisk surged nearly 12%, Semtech added 9.2%, and KLA Corp and Marvell Technology each rose more than 7%. FormFactor contributed a 7.4% gain in semiconductor equipment, underscoring broad-based strength throughout the chip supply chain. Industrials and Materials followed at fractional gains, while Homebuilders and Energy slipped modestly.

The session's sharpest pain landed in Software, which shed 1.25% as a group. Fair Isaac and UiPath each plunged more than 16%, Autodesk fell 8.3%, and Snowflake dropped 5.4%, suggesting earnings-season or guidance-related pressure weighing on the segment heading into the long weekend. Tesla retreated nearly 6%, adding an auto-sector coda to an otherwise chip-positive tape.

Traders return Tuesday to a market shaped by mounting geopolitical and inflation risks. Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic has fallen to its lowest level since May following exchanges of fire between U.S. and Iranian forces, diesel prices are flagged as a fresh threat to inflation expectations, and the Indian rupee required central-bank intervention to hold its footing. How energy markets process these pressures will set the tone for the shortened trading week.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Chokepoint Tightens After Naval Confrontations
briefs.body: Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to its lowest level since May after U.S. and Iranian forces traded strikes on ships in the region. Oil prices extended gains on the news, and analysts warn that any further escalation could compress an already strained global crude supply corridor.

briefs.headline: Iran Prepares New Maritime Restricted Zone in the Gulf
briefs.body: Tehran signaled it will announce a new restricted zone in the Persian Gulf within days, amplifying uncertainty for commercial shipping routes that carry a significant share of global oil exports. The move comes as Iranian authorities separately announced higher fuel prices for heavy domestic users.

briefs.headline: Diesel Prices Emerge as the Inflation Dove's Nemesis
briefs.body: Rising diesel costs are threatening to complicate the Federal Reserve's path toward easing, with analysts flagging the commodity as a particularly stubborn pass-through channel into freight and manufacturing costs. The dynamic could keep inflation readings elevated even as other price pressures ease.

briefs.headline: Rupee Steadied by Central Bank as Oil Strain Mounts
briefs.body: India's rupee came under selling pressure tied to elevated oil import costs but managed to stabilize after the Reserve Bank of India was reported by traders to have intervened in currency markets. The episode highlights how surging energy prices are rippling through emerging-market balance sheets.

briefs.headline: Ship Fuel Scarcity Risk Builds as Refiners Redirect Output
briefs.body: A potential shortage of marine fuel is emerging as war-related incentives push refiners to prioritize higher-margin products over bunker fuel. Shipping operators warn that tightening supply could raise freight costs and add another inflationary layer to global goods trade.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Stage Broad Friday Rally Ahead of Holiday Weekend
briefs.body: The semiconductor complex delivered one of its strongest single-session performances of the late summer, with memory, analog, and equipment names all posting significant gains on Friday. The advance stood in stark contrast to software peer losses, leaving investors to assess whether the chip rally has durable momentum heading into Tuesday's reopening.
